results.notes: Substrate MECHANICALLY CONFIRMED from corpus 17:1: asra = PERF 3MS + bi-'abdi-hi (3MS suffix) = 3rd-person opening; barak-NA = PERF 1P, li-nuriya = IMPF 1P SUBJ, ayati-NA = 1P suffix — the first-person cluster falls literally on the destination relative clause (alladhi barakna hawlahu, modifying al-masjid al-aqsa) and the purpose clause; inna-HU HUWA as-sami'u al-basir = 3MS return. The 3rd->1st->3rd ring is the literal segment order. But the four bundled tafsirs (Ibn Kathir, Tabari, Muyassar, Jalalayn) treat the isra' theologically and do NOT note a pronoun-ring whose near-point lands on the sacred destination — verified by cross_reference_tafsir. Ghayba<->takallum iltifat is a genuine named classical category; THIS structural reading is modern and must be flagged as such. Minor caution: classical ikhtilaf exists on the referent of innahu (Allah per Tabari/Jalalayn — follow them). Real but differentiable overlap with content/tadabbur/017-al-isra/ayahs-001-008.md (carried-motif, not the pronoun ring).
results.corrected: Frame explicitly as a modern structural/rhetorical reading offered as reflection: 'Classical balagha names this ghayba-to-takallum shift (iltifat); the observation that the first-person near-point falls exactly on destination+purpose is a modern structural reading the grammar supports, not something the classical mufassirun articulated.' Keep the grammatical facts stated as fact; downgrade the 'reserved exactly for the sacred moment' correspondence from revealed design to suggestive structural pattern.

results.notes: Substrate MECHANICALLY CONFIRMED from corpus 36:22: fatara = PERF 3MS + ni = PRON SUFF 1S ('created ME'); turja'una = IMPF VF:1 PASS 2MP + SUFF 2MP ('YOU-pl are returned') — genuine person mismatch (1S self-reference -> 2MP addressee) inside one coordinated clause; symmetry would demand 1S 'urja'u. 36:26 ya layta qawm-i carries the 1S suffix at 'my people'. RECOVERED in the tradition, verified via cross_reference_tafsir: al-Tabari glosses wa-ilayhi turja'un as 'wa-ilayhi tasiruna ANTUM ayyuha...' (the man turning to address his people); al-Jalalayn glosses fatarani with 'wa-antum kadhalik' and turja'un as 'ba'da al-mawt fa-yujazikum bi-kufrikum'; Ibn Kathir's rendering has 'to Whom YOU shall be returned'. The classical tradition explicitly saw the addressee turn. 'Grammar is the da'wah' is a light modern gloss on solid classical ground. Thematic overlap with content/tadabbur/036-ya-sin/ayahs-020-027.md is real but that file does not isolate the fatarani(1S) vs turja'un(2MP) grammatical hinge; differentiable. Strongest candidate of the batch.

Substrate MECHANICALLY CONFIRMED from corpus 12:29: a'rid = IMPV VF:4 2MS (to Yusuf); wa-staghfir-i = IMPV VF:10 2FS + li-dhanbi-KI (2FS) + inna-KI kun-TI (2FS) (to the wife); two successive imperatives, addressee flipped 2MS->2FS purely by morphology; no punitive clause on either — all correct. The COVER-UP reading is classically grounded, better than the candidate claimed: al-Jalalayn glosses a'rid as 'wa-la tadhkurhu li-alla yashi'a' (don't mention it lest it spread) and adds 'wa-shtahara al-khabar wa-sha'a'; al-Muyassar and Tabari likewise read 'don't tell anyone'; Ibn Kathir reads the man minimizing the scandal. THREE hedges required: (1) SPEAKER IKHTILAF — al-Tabari transmits from Ibn Abbas that the speaker of 12:29 is the household WITNESS (al-shahid), addressing both the woman and Yusuf; al-Muyassar and the common reading attribute it to the 'Aziz. The title/frame ('the Aziz issues two commands') must acknowledge this or soften the attribution. (2) NOT ILTIFAT PROPER — switching gender to address a man then a woman is ordinary Arabic address of two different people, not a person-shift device for a single referent; presenting it as addressee-iltifat overstates the balagha claim. (3) 'Grammar is the machinery of the cover-up' is a modern reflective layer on the classically-noted leniency. Weakest differentiation of the batch vs content/tadabbur/012-yusuf/ayahs-023-029.md (which already quotes a'rid); include only if the panel wants a dialogical specimen.
results.corrected: Lead with the classically-grounded point: two clipped commands and NO penalty on either party — the leniency and hush-up are what Ibn Kathir/al-Muyassar/al-Jalalayn note (Jalalayn: 'so it would not spread'). Present the masculine/feminine ending contrast as the audible texture of that asymmetry, NOT as rhetorical iltifat. Acknowledge the speaker ikhtilaf (the 'Aziz per most; the household witness per Ibn Abbas via Tabari) — e.g. 'the man of the house' framing. Flag 'grammar is the cover-up' as a modern reflective reading.
